title: Bright pixels along mesh edges when MSAA and glow are both enabled
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in 3.2.1 and 3.3-beta1. Not present in 3.1.4.

### System information

Windows 11, desktop renderer, dedicated GPU with current drivers

### Issue description

With 4x MSAA turned on in the project settings and glow enabled in the environment, every mesh that sits in front of a bright sky gets a one pixel fringe of white dots along its silhouette. The dots flicker when the camera moves. Turning off either MSAA or glow makes them vanish. It looks like the glow pass samples the unresolved multisample buffer.

### Steps to reproduce

1. New 3D scene with a cube, a sky and a camera.
2. Enable glow in the environment and set MSAA to 4x.
3. Run and look at the cube edges against the sky.

title: `await` never resumes if the signal fires in the same frame
body:
### Tested versions

3.3-beta1. Did not check 3.2.

### System information

Ubuntu 24.04, 16 GB RAM

### Issue description

If a function awaits a signal and that signal is emitted before the frame ends, the coroutine is never resumed. No error, the function just stays suspended forever. Emitting one frame later works fine. This breaks my loading screen because small levels finish loading instantly.

```
fn load_level():
    loader.start()
    await loader.finished
    print("never printed")
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Make a node with a signal `finished`.
2. In `start()` emit it right away.
3. Call the snippet above. The print is never reached.

title: Label with autowrap reports wrong minimum height inside a VBox
body:
### Tested versions

3.2.2, 3.3-beta1

### System information

macOS 15 on Apple silicon

### Issue description

A Label with autowrap enabled, placed in a VBox, reports the minimum height of a single line even when its text wraps to three or four lines. The container then lays out the next control on top of the wrapped text. Resizing the window by a pixel forces a relayout and everything snaps to the right place, so the size is computed correctly at some point, just too late.

### Steps to reproduce

1. VBox with a Label and a Button below it.
2. Give the Label a long sentence and turn on autowrap.
3. Run. The Button overlaps the second line of the text.

title: Hinge joint shakes violently when the two bodies have very different mass
body:
### Tested versions

3.3-beta1

### System information

Fedora 41, desktop renderer. Physics tick 60.

### Issue description

I'm building a crane. The arm is a RigidBody of mass 2 and the hook load has mass 400, linked with a HingeJoint. As soon as the simulation starts the joint vibrates, the bodies drift apart and after a few seconds the whole thing flies off into the distance. With equal masses the same setup is stable. Raising the solver iterations to 32 delays the explosion but doesn't prevent it.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Static anchor, RigidBody arm (mass 2), RigidBody load (mass 400).
2. Connect arm and load with a HingeJoint.
3. Run and wait about five seconds.

title: Dragging several selected nodes onto a new parent reverses their order
body:
### Tested versions

3.2.2 stable

### System information

Windows 10, 64-bit

### Issue description

Select three sibling nodes in the scene tree dock (A, B, C) and drag them onto another node. They end up as C, B, A under the new parent. For sprites that changes the draw order, so the scene looks different after what should be a pure reorganisation. Using the Reparent entry in the context menu keeps the order, only drag and drop is affected.

### Steps to reproduce

- Scene with nodes A, B, C as siblings and an empty node Group.
- Shift-select A to C in the scene tree dock.
- Drag onto Group and look at the order.

title: Mobile renderer draws semi-transparent sprites behind opaque ones when Y-sort is enabled
body:
### Tested versions

3.3-beta1, mobile renderer. Desktop renderer is fine.

### System information

macOS 14, tested in the editor with the mobile renderer selected

### Issue description

After enabling Y-sort on the parent node, sprites whose texture has partial alpha (glass, smoke puffs) are drawn underneath fully opaque sprites that should be behind them. It seems the mobile renderer puts all blended items into one batch and draws it before the opaque batch instead of after. Switching the project to the desktop renderer gives correct ordering with the same scene.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Parent node with Y-sort on.
2. Add an opaque crate sprite and a semi-transparent window sprite lower on screen.
3. Run with the mobile renderer. The window is hidden by the crate.

title: Audible click at the loop point of OGG streams
body:
### Tested versions

3.2.1, 3.2.2, 3.3-beta1

### System information

Windows 11, onboard sound, headphones

### Issue description

Looping an OGG stream produces a short click every time playback wraps around. The file itself loops cleanly in an audio editor, sample-accurate, so I think the engine drops or repeats a few samples at the seam. The WAV version of the same clip loops without any click. Changing the loop offset doesn't help. Very noticeable with ambient pads.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Import a seamless OGG and tick Loop in the import dock.
2. Play it on an AudioPlayer routed to the Master bus.
3. Listen at the loop point.

title: Script editor autocomplete shows nothing for variables with inferred type
body:
### Tested versions

3.2.2

### System information

Ubuntu 22.04

### Issue description

In the script editor, code completion doesn't list members for variables declared with `:=`. For `var body: RigidBody = ...` typing `body.` pops up the list as expected. For `var body := get_node("Crate") as RigidBody` the popup stays empty, although the LarkScript analyzer clearly knows the type, because hovering the name shows RigidBody in the tooltip.

### Steps to reproduce

Open any script, type the two declarations, then type `body.` after each one and compare the completion popup.

title: CharacterBody creeps down slopes while standing still
body:
### Tested versions

3.2.2 and 3.3-beta1 both

### System information

Windows 11 laptop, integrated graphics (shouldn't matter)

### Issue description

A CharacterBody standing on a 30 degree ramp with zero input velocity slowly slides downhill, about a pixel every few frames in 2D. `stop_on_slope` is enabled and the floor max angle is 45. It only stops completely if I set gravity to zero while grounded, which is a hack. It seems gravity is applied before the floor snap and leaves a tiny leftover motion each tick.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Static ramp at 30 degrees.
2. CharacterBody with the default movement template, `stop_on_slope` on.
3. Walk onto the ramp, release all keys and print the position each tick.

title: Typed array accepts the wrong element type through an untyped reference
body:
### Tested versions

3.2.2

### System information

Debian 12

### Issue description

An `Array[int]` can be filled with strings if it is first assigned to an untyped variable. No error at parse time, no error at runtime on append. The crash arrives much later when something iterates the array and does arithmetic.

```
var scores: Array[int] = []
var anything = scores
anything.append("oops")
```

I expected the append to raise a type error, since the underlying array is still typed.

### Steps to reproduce

Run the three lines in any `_ready`. Afterwards `for s in scores: print(s + 1)` fails with an operand error, far away from the real mistake.

title: ScrollPanel jumps back to the top whenever a child is added
body:
### Tested versions

3.2.1 through 3.3-beta1

### System information

macOS 15

### Issue description

Adding a control to the VBox inside a ScrollPanel resets the vertical scroll offset to 0. Users reading older entries in a long list get thrown back to the top each time a new row arrives. Saving `scroll_offset` and restoring it after the add works only if deferred by a frame, and it causes a visible flash.

### Steps to reproduce

1. ScrollPanel > VBox with 50 Labels.
2. Scroll halfway down.
3. From a timer, add another Label to the VBox every second.
4. The view jumps to the top on each add.

title: Crackling output on Windows when the device runs at 48 kHz and the mix rate is 44.1 kHz
body:
### Tested versions

3.2.2

### System information

Windows 11, USB audio interface set to 48000 Hz in the sound control panel

### Issue description

All audio crackles, a fine static on top of everything, when the Windows output device is set to 48 kHz while the project mix rate is left at the default 44100. Setting the mix rate to 48000 or switching the device to 44.1 kHz cleans it up. The same project on Linux with the same interface has no crackle, so I suspect the resampler in the Windows audio driver path.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Set the output device to 48 kHz in Windows.
2. Play any stream on the Master bus.
3. Crackle is audible immediately, also in the editor preview.

title: Editor crashes on launch under Wayland with fractional scaling
body:
### Tested versions

3.3-beta1. 3.2.2 starts fine on the same machine.

### System information

Fedora 41, Wayland session, display scale 125%

### Issue description

The editor window opens for a split second and then the process dies. With the scale set to 100% or 200% it starts normally, and forcing X11 through the command line flag also works. Terminal output ends with:

```
ERROR: surface size 0x0 is not valid for scale 1.25
```

The project manager is affected too, so it happens before any project is loaded.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Set the desktop display scale to 125%.
2. Start the editor in a Wayland session.
3. Crash right after the window appears.

title: Web export: textures with non power of two size turn black when mipmaps are on
body:

3.2.2 web export, Chrome and Firefox

### System information

Windows 11 host, exported with the mobile renderer on WebGL 2

### Issue description

In the web export, any texture whose dimensions are not a power of two renders solid black as soon as mipmaps are enabled in its import settings. Desktop exports of the same project show the texture correctly. Disabling mipmaps or resizing the image to 512x512 fixes it. The browser console prints a warning about an incomplete texture.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Import a 300x200 PNG with mipmaps enabled.
2. Put it on a sprite.
3. Export to web and open the page.

title: Calling `move_and_collide` from a `body_entered` handler errors out
body:
### Tested versions

3.3-beta1

### System information

Ubuntu 24.04

### Issue description

Calling `move_and_collide` on another body inside a `body_entered` handler prints this and the move is dropped:

```
ERROR: cannot modify physics space while queries are being flushed
```

From LarkScript there is no way to tell that the signal is emitted in the middle of the physics step. Either the call should be queued automatically or the error should mention `call_deferred`, which works around it.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Trigger area with a script connected to `body_entered`.
2. In the handler call `other.move_and_collide(Vector2(0, -8))`.
3. Let a body enter the area.

title: Reverb effect on a bus keeps ringing after its wet level is set to zero

macOS 15

title: Tile map editor: rectangle tool paints one cell off when zoomed out

3.3-beta1, also 3.2.2

Linux Mint 22

In the tile map editor, the rectangle tool places the painted area one cell to the right and down from the preview outline once the viewport zoom is below 50%. title: `File.open` fails on Windows when the user folder name has non-ASCII characters
body:
### Tested versions

3.2.2

### System information

Windows 10, account name contains accented letters

### Issue description

Saving the game does not work for one of our testers. His Windows account name has an accented letter, so the user data path contains it too. `File.open("user://save.dat", File.WRITE)` returns null and `File.last_error()` says the path was not found. On my machine with a plain ASCII account name the same build saves fine. Looks like the path is converted with the wrong code page somewhere.

1. Create a Windows account with an accented letter in its name.
2. Run a script that opens a file under `user://` for writing.
3. The call returns null.

title: Fast RigidBody tunnels through thin static colliders even with continuous detection
body:
### Tested versions

3.2.2, 3.3-beta1

### System information

Ubuntu 24.04, physics tick 60

### Issue description

A small RigidBody moving at around 3000 units per second passes straight through a static collider that is 4 units thick. Continuous collision detection is set to the shape-cast mode on the body, which is supposed to prevent exactly this. Raising the physics tick rate to 240 hides the problem but is too expensive. Thick colliders stop the body as expected.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Static box collider, 4 units thick.
2. RigidBody sphere with continuous detection enabled.
3. Apply an impulse so it reaches about 3000 units per second towards the box.
4. It ends up on the other side.

title: Garbled pink textures on some Android phones with the mobile renderer

3.3-beta1 Android export

Two budget phones on Android 13. A newer Android 15 device is fine.

title: Hover font colour override is ignored on toggle Buttons while they are pressed

macOS 14

I set theme overrides on a Button with toggle mode: font colour, font hover colour and font pressed colour. When the button is toggled on and the mouse hovers it, the text uses the plain pressed colour instead of the hover one, so there is no hover feedback at all on active buttons. title: No sound after resuming from suspend on Linux with PipeWire
body:

3.2.2, 3.3-beta1

### System information

Arch Linux, PipeWire, laptop speakers

### Issue description

If the laptop is suspended while the editor or a running game is open, there is no audio output after waking up. The mixer panel still shows the level meters moving on every bus, so streams are playing, but nothing reaches the speakers. Other applications have sound. Only restarting the engine brings audio back. I could not reproduce it on a desktop machine that uses a different sound server, so somebody else should confirm.

1. Play a looping stream.
2. Suspend the machine and wake it up.
3. Silence, meters still move.

title: Chat log loses its place every time a message arrives
body:

3.3-beta1

Windows 11

### Issue description

Our in-game chat is a scrollable column of message rows. When a player has scrolled up to read older messages and a new one is appended at the bottom, the view snaps all the way back to the very first message. During a busy match it is impossible to read anything. I expected the view to stay where it is unless the player was already at the bottom.

1. Fill a scrollable list with rows.
2. Scroll somewhere in the middle.
3. Append a row from code.
4. The view is at the first row again.

title: Raycast misses collision shapes on nodes with non-uniform scale
body:
### Tested versions

3.2.1, 3.2.2

### System information

Windows 11

### Issue description

Raycasts go through a box collision shape when its parent body is scaled non-uniformly, for example (3, 1, 1). The debug draw shows the collider stretched as expected, and rigid bodies do collide with the stretched shape, but `raycast()` only hits the region the shape would occupy at scale 1. With a uniform scale of 3 the ray hits correctly everywhere.

1. Static body with a box shape, scale it to (3, 1, 1).
2. Cast a ray at the outer third of the box.
3. The result is empty.

title: Reordering buses by dragging in the audio dock leaves their effects on the old slot

title: Debugger skips breakpoints placed after an `await`

Fedora 40

macOS 15

title: GPU particles stop emitting for good after the scene tree is paused and resumed
body:

3.2.2, 3.3-beta1

title: Game is laggy

3.2.2

title: `match` with a dictionary pattern falls through to the wildcard branch
body:
### Tested versions

3.3.1

### System information

Debian 12

### Issue description

A dictionary pattern in a `match` statement never matches when the matched value has more keys than the pattern, even with the open-ended `..` marker.

```
match {"kind": "door", "locked": true}:
    {"kind": "door", ..}:
        print("door")
    _:
        print("other")   # this runs
```

Without the extra key the first branch is taken. The language reference says `..` allows additional keys.

### Steps to reproduce

Run the snippet in a script.
